questions.q: What does Kumalo buy for Gertrude to replace her dirty clothes?
choices: A red dress and a white turban for her head
questions.explain: He also buys a shirt, short trousers and a jersey for the boy, though his own frayed collars must wait.

questions.q: How is Kumalo's brother John sitting when they arrive at his shop?
choices: On a chair 'like a chief', talking to two other men
questions.explain: John has grown fat and sits with his hands on his knees, a man of importance in Sophiatown.

questions.q: Why does John say he stopped writing home and stopped going to church?
choices: He lost his faith after an illness
In Johannesburg he has become 'a man of some importance', free of the chief — and the Church, he says, 'is like the chief'
questions.explain: John insists on speaking English to explain his 'experience': the tribal society is breaking apart and a new society is being built in Johannesburg.

questions.q: What happened to John's wife Esther?
choices: She left him ten years ago; he now lives with another woman
She returned to Ndotsheni with the children
questions.explain: Msimangu coldly suggests Esther 'believed in fidelity', a word John does not recognise.

questions.q: According to John, what is Johannesburg — and South Africa — really built on?
choices: The backs, sweat and labour of black workers paid three shillings a day
questions.explain: 'It is not built on the mines... it is built on our backs, on our sweat, on our labour.'

questions.q: Where does John say Absalom and his own son went to work?
choices: A factory — the Doornfontein Textiles Company, 14 Krause Street
questions.explain: John looks the address up in the telephone book; he cannot simply phone, 'They do not do such things for a black man.'

questions.q: What does Msimangu say is the one thing that 'has power completely'?
choices: Love — 'because when a man loves, he seeks no power, and therefore he has power'
questions.explain: He warns that a man who gets power and money is often corrupted and comes to enjoy them for their own sake.

choices: That 'one day when they are turned to loving, they will find we are turned to hating'
That he will lose his faith
questions.explain: He fears the white man will come to love justice only after the black man has given up on it.

questions.q: Where do they learn Absalom went after leaving the factory about a year before?
choices: To stay with Mrs Ndlela at 105 End Street, Sophiatown
questions.explain: A workman, Dhlamini, remembers Absalom was friendly with him and gives Mrs Ndlela's address.

questions.q: What forwarding address does Mrs Ndlela's letter from Absalom give?
choices: c/o Mrs Mkize, 79 Twenty-Third Avenue, Alexandra
questions.explain: Mrs Ndlela looks at Kumalo 'half with pity'; she 'did not like his son's friends', which is why Absalom left her house.
